title: Decision from one-sided error
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every run on every binary input uses space at most $s$ of its input length. For each input $x$, suppose there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, the probability of outputting $1$ is at least $2/3$ if $x\in L$, and every length-$T$ branch outputs $0$ if $x\notin L$. Then for every input $x$, there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, every length-$T$ branch uses space at most $s(|x|)$, and $x\in L$ exactly when some length-$T$ branch halts with output $1$.

$L$ is a language of binary strings
$s$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers

On nonmembers, every length-$T$ choice word produces output $0$
